verdict.tagline: Rough performance hides a sprawling and replayable shooter
for_you_if: you want deeply replayable co-op combat
you enjoy hunting for obscure secrets
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you want clear in-game guidance for puzzles

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment shifts upward significantly as playtime increases from the opening hours into the endgame.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players encounter severe technical instability, startup crashes, and blocking bugs.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues including game freezes, lag spikes, and long loading times on startup.

citations.review_text:
If the first five minutes I would recommend this game, but after that this in-game part became a joke to withstand.

The first problem are the game freeze and lag spike over and over, and the huge times when loading the game on start, another big issue are the maps guiding system that couldn't found the NPC in-game, when in battle you can't found the next key place too.

When come to the coop mode the whole game became disaster, this game already need huge time loading and this time became double in coop, since there only one hp bar, so when you fall down then die the whole match you end and can't got anything.

The story part seem the main advertisement for this game, but combined all above problem into this game, the story are you click over and over in all option dialog, just see the NPC dialog then move to next maps, that the sad news and ruined this game immersive.

If you are looking for a punishing, dark, atmospheric challenge that tests your mechanical skill and positioning like a proper FromSoftware title, you’ve been aggressively lied to. The marketing team pushing the "Dark Souls with guns" narrative needs to be banned from the industry for life.

Here is the unoptimized reality of this game:

Performance is a joke: This game doesn't run; it struggles to survive on your hardware. The frame drops are completely erratic. It feels like the backend was held together by pure hope and duct tape. If you don't turn on three different upscalers simultaneously, your rig will literally melt before it achieves a stable frame rate.

Visuals from 2015: The funniest part about the hardware demands is that the game looks ancient. The textures are flat, the environments feel plastic, and the overall visual fidelity reminds me of a mediocre mid-tier PS4 title rather than anything modern. There is absolutely no justification for this level of poor optimization.

Where are the Souls-like elements? Nowhere. Instead of a deep, rewarding combat system, intricate level design, or genuine atmosphere, you get a mindless, repetitive looter-shooter. This isn't a Souls game; it's a gray, depressing, uninspired Borderlands clone where challenge is replaced by an artificial, boring grind and endless waves of generic trash mobs.

If you aren't a fan of DLLS, upscaling, and frame generation stay far away. The game looked like a blurry pile of it so I turned off DLLS like I do in all games and usually I go from high to mediums and maybe some low shadows and foliage to get 100+ FPS on these newer titles. Remnant runs at all lows at an unstable 60fps, it feels terrible. 

I'm not usually one to complain about playing on lows but that was when I owned a potato, to be forced to play on settings labeled "potato" with the specs I have and not even have a stable 60fps at 1080p shows the incompetence that AI upscaling and frame generation brings. 

A lack of optimization and a disregard for the functional state of the game in favor of cost saving. The end user (you) receives a worse product and experience.

Say no to AI in our games and lives, do not use AI nor promote it, refund games that abuse AI generation to worsen our favorite characters, stories, and experiences. 

Its a shame I was told this game was better than the first as far as the gameplay experience but I cannot look beyond the horrendous performance issues caused by a cheap developers who don't care for the end user.

DLLS, frame generation, upscaling, it all looks like trash. I notice it instantly.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience severe crashes and lockups that prevent the game from running properly.

citations.review_text: This game did not launch no matter what, I spent hours trying to clear cashe's, update compatability, make sure everything on my computer was up to date and correctly working. didn't matter. got maybe 10 minutes of play time, the other 30 were spent constantly opening and closing the game due to crashes and self shutdown. It seems enjoyable and fun, but I have yet for the game to actually launch.

I admit that I have an odd system configuration; however, when every single game in my somewhat considerable library runs, and this one not only crashes so hard that I am unable to close the program, I am also unable to use any of my inputs, even to exit to tty. It crashes so hard that even after killing the process by remote SSH connection, the PC remains locked up. Impressively, even after I kill all graphics, the TTY is STILL SLUGGISH.
I must unfortunately conclude, that if this course of events is at all possible, some developer along the pipeline has tremendously ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.

I once spent over a year troubleshooting a single game on and off. It was at least well behaved enough to crash.
This garbage has impressed me by being so broken from the get-go that I am unwilling to even work with it.

Dark Souls with guns and coop sounds really fun. For the love of God fix the tech.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the opening section of the game features lengthy cutscenes and dialogue sequences.

citations.review_text:
This is the most random and aimless game ive ever seen. It does not build on remnant 1 in a significant way that demands an entire sequel. the gunplay and combat is the exact same as the first game, but its just filled with this all this random trash. terrible story. terrible nonsensical cut scenes, etc. You start out in a "the last of us" style post apoc city, then you're in a sewer, then you're in an unnecessarily large hub, then all the sudden you're in an alien halo reach world with robot glider things. 

At that point i had to stop myself and ask "what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on" it is just all over the place with the story and cutscene spamming. It feels like its trying to do and be a bunch of things at once but very softly delivering on all of it.

By the time i actually got to the first few check points i just had to stop playing it. it doesn't feel rewarding or impactful or good to play. 4/10 painfully average

This game hasnt bored me this much in a while. just run past all the enemies, the intro is just cutscene spam and walking simulator and the puzzles think im the smartest man alive. The voice acting makes me wanna turn my volume off at how much they whine. Remnant 1 was way better

citations.review_text: Very disappointed in this. No controller remapping in 2026 is a deal breaker.

it showcases the performance difference of "new" and old games, using some corridors and even those areas have low performance. hard to run on old cards even at 720p and if using upscaling. very big file size 80-90gb.

gameplay is okey/fun, could be too annoying at times.
story/dialogue is like "living with a black old dude, how odd!", with story progression being too slow (more so in the tutorial). some areas can be hard to see what is going on and controls can sometimes be weird on KB and Mouse.

would be a mixed review, but combat doesn't seem too bad and might change my tune later.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the story and voice acting as poor, with dialogue that feels like advertisement reads.

citations.review_text:
Buy it cheap if you do, lots of replay value if you like to be punished for existing. The initial few hours is pretty interesting, everything feels strange and novel and like discovering something. Story is horrid and voice acting direction is completely wrong. It all sounds like ad reads. Problems show up quick when you start to want to dig into mechanics and tailor builds to suit your playstyle, suddenly it all falls apart. Also when you realize the way the devs expect you to play the game, i.e. puzzles. you realize how narrow their design vision was.

I will never appreciate difficulty that stems from poor design. The game is in DESPERATE need of both movement speed and reload speed enhancements. The devs actively went out of their way to remove these as there are many places for them, particularly since the looter shooter genre is a standard now. No buffs for armor sets or individual pieces? Cool, would have been a nice way to allow players to tailor the game to their tastes. I'm not looking for easy, when it works well its really engaging, but when it stumbles over itself its absolutely insulting. There is a place where you fight an enemy high up, during that fight you can see where you need to shoot but THE GAME WONT LET YOU AIM UP FAR ENOUGH, you literally cannot aim within the range of any normal human. Reloading is PAINFULLY slow, sprint regularly fails to trigger despite the button press and it feels like your character is constantly moving as slowly as possible. Its all just a slog to play, and its heavily balanced towards coop - with little thought to single player. I'm often left wishing for things like shields or other mechanics (there are shields but they are a joke) to help offset the lack of coop teammates. The amount of fiddling you have to do to manage health and gameplay mechanics is unreal, especially with no pause or pause-select type functions. Healing animation takes 5 years to complete and any little pebble or gust of wind interrupts it. The…

Very low variety of enemies per level, boring progression, bare bones story with some of the worst voive acting i have ever heard. Characters i just don't care about and dialouge that just goes on forver just to say nothing.

The gun play is good, and thats about it.

The game also runs bad for somthing that looks like a slightly better fallout 4 with no option to turn off depth of field.

It's also another black woman strong White man dumb and weak slop woke game.

3/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that movement animations and traversal objects like ladders, doors, and elevators feel slow and act as time wasters.

citations.review_text:
Honestly... the Gunplay is kinda fun. 

But there's not enough guns. There's too much backtracking and it's hard to figure out where to go. A lot of wasted time waiting for elevators and doors to open and then close on you, forcing you to run out and back to reset the door. At least it's not intuitive for me to figure it out.

The bosses and combat is fun, but again, the direction provided is weak and lacks the polish you'd expect.

Can't recommend.

Just to much... Tediousness?  It just has a lot of unfun design.

You have to backtrack a lot.  Through some pretty annoying level designs.  Like slow ladders, doors that take forever, this awful glider/updraft system, elevator animations, campfire animations.  Basically a lot of time wasters.  it feels like non-combat animations were designed to slow the game down in a really frustrating way.

Some of the UIs are clunky.  Like joining a friends game, or "fast travelin" around the map if you can call it that.

The controls aren't the worst I've ever experienced but they are subpar.  Talking to NPCs or shopping should be much easier.  You can't jump, except when the game 'allows' you to for instance - in a game with LOTS of verticality.  Cant bind your weapons, you have to mousewheel or cycle through them.  Stuff like that.  

Like nothing game breaking - but it all adds up to enough levels of frustration to drown out the joy that games are meant to bring.

There are things I like.  The art team killed it.  Really cool monster designs.  The weapons and builds seem diverse and there is a lot agency you have making your character choices.  The combat is good.  I'd give the combat a 6.5 out of 10.  Solid and enjoyable.

But all the good bits are just weighted down by... choices.

For me? No matter how good, this combination of souls-like bosses, grind, puzzles and pretty much zero story makes this game more bitter than sweet.

Co op centric souls-like with guns that has an absurd amount of secrets to find. What's not to like? This game is ridiculously fun if you have people to play with. My biggest gripes are that the game is very ugly by default (can be improved in settings big time) and that some of the 'secrets' are so insanely obscure that you need to look up datamined solutions. These, however, make up a very small portion of the hidden rewards, and you can solve most by yourself with a good head on your shoulders. 10/10 I hope we get a Remnant 3.

REMNANT II is an action shooter centered on world-hopping survival. After saving a single world in the first game, the stakes are cranked up—now you're tasked with saving the entire multiverse using the giant red Worldstone.

[b] The Short Answer: Is It Worth Buying?[/b]
If you genuinely enjoy hunting down obscure secrets, solving puzzles, and tight third-person shooting, it’s worth picking up. Otherwise, it’s probably not worth your time.

[b] Do You Need a Wiki?[/b]
If you actually want to figure out what's hidden in the worlds and unlock secrets, then yes—absolutely.

[b] Playtime [/b] 5/10
The main campaign takes around 20–25 hours, while any additional time depends entirely on how much you want to level up your builds and hunt down gear.

[b] Story[/b] 5/10
In the first game, you saved one world; now you have to save everything using the red stone.

[b] Music[/b] 4/10
It’s not bad by any means, but after about 3 hours, it starts getting repetitive and wearing on your nerves.

[b] Graphics[/b] 5/10
Solid AA quality presentation.

[b] Mechanics[/b] 5/10
The gunplay is genuinely very good. There are several base archetypes (classes) to choose from, alongside a bunch of secret hidden classes that require specific, secret steps to unlock. On the downside, enemy design within each world feels repetitive—aside from the 3rd world, most mobs play identically despite having different models.
Exploration logic often feels absent; you'll naturally expect a chest, crate, or barrel around a dead-end turn, only to find completely empty space—not even a breakable pot. The core loop relies on dynamic generation where every Adventure mode roll builds a unique combination of locations, maps, and events (though for a single campaign run, this doesn't matter much). Primary weapon variety felt very lacking; I effectively ran through the entire game with the starting rifle (mainly because there wasn't a proper marksman rifle that fit my specific style). Sidearms, on the other hand, o…

citations.review_text:
[h1] ReMIDnant 2 [/h1]

boss fight are 7/10 at best 

But the mapping part... The game has zero enemy placement design. There’s nothing happens for awhile and then... the music starts, and enemies literally spawn from behind you and two other corners. It feels so lazy.

The story are so so but the dialogue...  Holy ♥♥♥♥! Are those Chatgpt before Chatgpt even a thing? >:(

This is a hesitant and caveated yes, if you have someone to play through the whole game with you.

I wanted to love the game as the gameplay and art direction is incredible, however the story/writing comes across as "Millennial marvel quips" galore, completely ruining the serious tone and direction. It is beyond me why they did this. We spent the entire playthrough rolling our eyes at some of the nonsense the main character spews. 

Gameplay is fun enough, but was a bit disappointed by the lack of armour/guns. It's incredibly depressing to basically not find any upgrades to your starting gear throughout the main campaign. I chose challenger as my class and I didn't find anything remotely better than what I was given at the start of the game until near the last boss, so there wasn't much "carrot on a stick" for me to keep playing post game. I feel like the game would have benefitted a lot more from having a heavier looter shooter loot system, which would have incentivised me more to keep playing.

Puzzles are really cool and enjoyable, kind of fun to play something that actually puts a challenge in the puzzles without splashing yellow paint everywhere.

The worlds are really neat and again, I cannot commend the art direction enough, however I would have loved for the game to have one or two more maps than the 3 adventure mode selections.

The most Born of Osiris eqsue games I've played in my recent memory. If you're a fan of some of the bands signed under Sumerian Records, Remnant 2 will hypnotize you

The dialogue writing and voice acting is done by 5 year olds however, literally every human (INCLUDING THE MAIN CHARACTER) talks like they have an underdeveloped prefrontal cortex. Its a shame you have to sit through so much  corniness to enjoy this otherwise amazing amazing game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features random world generation and procedural layouts, which enables campaign re-rolling and finding new secrets across playthroughs.

citations.review_text:
Remnant 2- What can I say? It is a game steeped in mixed controversy, opinions, and results on various different consoles and parts. It is said to have many bugs, errors, and problems; and some even say it's been abandoned- not even affording the same positivity that Remnant 1 gets however many do agree it is a good game for its own reasons and some things most will agree on is the replayability factor the game has.

- You can spend much time in the game and still find a new secret, game mechanic, or new way to play.

- It is a great replay-ability factor, even upon finishing your campaign you can re-roll it and start over with a new play, new possibilities, and options for loot you never had the chance to get before when used with adventure mode too.

- You have different difficulties to play upwards to apocalypse, and yes; even hardcore mode where you die even once your entire save gets delated. This is more advised after playing normally on a separate character, unlocking all your archtypes, your different difficulty accomplishments up to apocalypse because each difficulty as a different set of rewards for complete I believe, and anything your character accomplishes and clears in that regard- your hardcore character can buy those cleared rewards in weapons from the merchants at Ward 13 to start however you want. That is of course when you can afford them and the upgrades.

- Plenty of ways to build your traits when you get enough, plenty of rings, amulets, armors, and weapons to mix up and try out. Will your build be good and carry you far? That takes time, hunting, and lots of loot and traits to figure out and if nothing else there are plenty communities out there that can offer insight.

- In my 30 hours of gameplay I have experienced no bugs or issues and I am playing on a brand new Lenovo legion 5 with 1TB Hard-drive though I am sure I have a solid SSD as well that helps. It plays well on the graphics auto-set. Max? No, but still looks good and play…

I personally had a great time playing, the game impressed me with its challenging combat, interesting world design, and the amount of freedom it gives players to build their characters. Whether playing solo or with friends, every run felt exciting because the game constantly surprised me with new enemies, locations, and rewards.

   I liked how each world feels unique and has its own atmosphere, secrets, and puzzles. The procedural generation keeps things fresh, making repeat playthroughs worthwhile instead of feeling repetitive. The boss fights are another highlight—they're challenging, creative, and satisfying to overcome after learning their mechanics.

I also liked the variety of weapons, archetypes, and character builds. There are so many ways to customize your playstyle that experimenting never gets old. The progression system rewards exploration, and discovering hidden items or secret areas is always satisfying.

I personally also appreciated the co-op experience. Playing with friends makes difficult encounters more enjoyable, and teamwork adds another layer of strategy. Even when playing alone, the game remains engaging thanks to its balanced difficulty.

I disliked that the difficulty can sometimes feel overwhelming, especially for new players. Some boss fights may require multiple attempts before figuring out the right strategy, which can be frustrating. I also disliked that important items or quests can be easy to miss because of the game's randomly generated worlds, sometimes requiring additional playthroughs.

 Pros
+ Excellent and satisfying combat.
+ Great variety of weapons and character builds.
+ Unique worlds with strong replay value.
+ Challenging and memorable boss fights.
+ Fun and rewarding co-op gameplay.
+ Lots and LOTS of secrets, puzzles, and exploration.

Cons
- Can be very difficult for newcomers and many mobs have too many stun attacks.
- Random generation may hide important content and you have to retry generate another one...
- Some…

I've been playing this game since it was released, first on PS5, now on my gaming PC. Not only is this one of the greatest games I have ever played, it is also the most re-playable game I have ever played. If you like souls like games and you love shooters, look no further. The builds, game play, bosses, insane way it re-rolls campaigns-- there just isn't anything like it! Graphics- check. Amazing re-rollable campaigns- check. Interesting non-campaign play options- check. Great coop play option- check. Superb gun play with options of mele, souls like dodging/rolling- check. Deep RPG builds/loot- check. Interesting story- check. I could keep going on, but you get the point. Play Remnant II!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues, including random stutters and frame rate drops in certain areas and DLC maps.

citations.review_text:
I really liked Remnant 2 overall. I played through the game on Veteran difficulty and honestly, the gameplay is probably the strongest part of it. The gunplay feels even smoother than Remnant 1, the weapons have more impact, and the movement and combat just feel really good. Shooting, dodging, switching weapons and messing around with different builds is genuinely fun.

But man, the optimization is rough. Some areas run perfectly fine and then you enter certain DLC maps and the performance just falls apart. The random stutters and FPS drops really take away from the experience, especially during fights where every frame matters.

Another thing I really wish they did better is the bosses. I'm not even comparing them to other Soulslikes, but after beating a lot of the bosses, I rarely got that "holy sh*t, I actually did it" feeling. Some fights are cool mechanically, but none of them felt truly iconic or memorable to me. I wish the bosses had more personality and those moments that stick with you long after the fight is over.

The story is also nothing special, and the procedural nature of the game can sometimes make exploration feel a little repetitive. The progression and traits aren't always that exciting either.

Still, I'd recommend Remnant 2. The core gameplay is just too much fun to ignore. It has some rough edges, but when everything clicks, it's a really damn good shooter.

How have I NOT left a review for this game yet...? This game is absolute peak. Everything (except story...) is top notch. It's super fun solo or with friends, definitely give this game a try. Play the first game if you haven't already, they're both fantastic. Even with the cons, game is definitely worth a shot, get the DLC if you're going in.

I will say performance is lacking on the PC version of this game, sometimes. Quite a bit of stuttering and crashes. Control wise, gunplay is better on M&K, but everything else feels better on controller. Overall, console is a better experience, IMO.

Nonetheless, I've played a lot on here and PS5 and it's one of my favorite games of all time. Super replayable, very fun alone or with others, it's just a great time. Get the deluxe and say bye to days of your life!

9.5/10 game.
